subject: Ownership boundary decisions — output title vs. training & feedback license
messages:

Subject: MSA redlines (output/training) — draft attached

Hi Neha,

Attached is Acme Health's mark-up of the MSA and Order Form focused on the sections that mention output ownership and derivative use. High level: customer wants explicit assignment of outputs generated by the service for their productization, and they are proposing a narrow training carve-out that allows them to opt-in for telemetry uploads to a customer dataset.

Two asks for you and Laura:
- Can Redwood confirm whether current runtime logs/telemetry would be considered data subject to an opt-in training license in the draft?
- We flagged the feedback/license paragraph (Section 7.2) and suggested a version that assigns output title to Acme but grants Redwood a nonexclusive internal research license.

I included Olivia from Product so she can weigh in on the productization angle. Ben

Subject: Re: MSA redlines (output/training) — draft attached

Ben / Olivia — thanks for the redline. Quick internal read and proposed approach below. I also attached a 1-page summary for Legal & Sales to propose back.

Key points from our side:
1) Output title vs. service license: we can accept customer ownership of "Customer Outputs" that are direct responses to customer inputs for their product (explicitly defined), but we need to preserve a scoped service-rights clause that allows Redwood to run the hosted service, monitor performance, and de-bug. That should be a narrow, noncommercial service license, not a broad research/training right.

2) Training telemetry opt-in: runtime telemetry (latency, token counts, anonymized failure logs) is operational — we can agree to exclude that from any training license. Any dataset used for model training must be an opt-in export that Acme explicitly sends to Redwood and is time-stamped and documented in the order form (we propose an Exhibit).

3) Feedback license: we cannot accept assignment of feedback to the customer. We can offer a limited feedback license back to Redwood (nonexclusive, royalty-free) for product improvement but explicitly exclude downstream productization that uses Acme proprietary prompts or proprietary outputs.

Proposed next steps:
- Laura / Connor: legal team to draft counter-proposals for Section 4 (Outputs) and Section 7 (Feedback/Training). I've highlighted required guardrails in the attached summary.
- Suggest a 1-hour sync with Acme legal + product this week to walk the proposed language and the Exhibit model for telemetry/training opt-in.

I can be on the call — what times work for Acme?

Thanks,

Neha — appreciate the quick read. A couple clarifications from Acme: we can accept a "service operation" privilege but need stronger language to prevent Redwood from using Customer Outputs for model training even after minimization/anonymization. Our product team is worried about derivative models being trained on outputs that include patient-facing templates.

If Redwood can provide the Exhibit approach (explicit opt-in export + audit trail) and accept an express non-training covenant for Customer Outputs, Acme will be willing to scale back the assignment language in Section 4.

We are available for a sync Thu 10–12 PT or Fri 09–11 PT. Ben

Team — short plan before the sync with Acme:
- Connor to draft counter-language for Section 4 ("Customer Outputs") that:
  * Defines Customer Outputs narrowly (responses generated only from Customer Inputs and customer-provided assets).
  * Explicitly carves out runtime telemetry and anonymized operational metrics.
- I will draft a proposed Exhibit A for telemetry/training opt-in which records what files/data constitute an "export" and the paperwork/audit-trail required.
- Neha to lead the sync and present the non-training covenant (we do not accept broad training rights absent an explicit opt-in export).

Connor — target 3 proposed bullets for Section 4 by EOD today so I can fold into Exhibit draft.
